claim_verbatim: At this pace, it will take 187 years to extract enough copper for the energy transition.
resolution_criterion: Arithmetic illustration at stated pace, not a prediction that the transition waits 187 years.
resolution_rule_fixed: Arithmetic illustration at stated pace, not a prediction that the transition waits 187 years.
notes: Counterfactual pace math; unscorable as event forecast.

claim_verbatim: Chilean copper disruption; Peru watch — Medium–High. Chilean interruptions and the Caserones guidance reduction are observed. Further disruption depends on damage to access, power or transport.
source: Essay: The 1/1000 Year El Niño Almanac
resolution_criterion: YES if Chile/Peru copper ops report additional material weather-related disruptions or guidance cuts over Sep 2026–Mar 2027 beyond already-observed Caserones cut; NO if operations normalize without further material cuts.
resolution_rule_fixed: YES if Chile/Peru copper ops report additional material weather-related disruptions or guidance cuts over Sep 2026–Mar 2027 beyond already-observed Caserones cut; NO if operations normalize without further material cuts.

claim_verbatim: Southern African maize — Medium–High. The regional outlook favours drier conditions during the 2026–27 growing season. Yield losses could increase import requirements.
source: Essay: The 1/1000 Year El Niño Almanac
resolution_criterion: YES if Southern African maize yields for 2026/27 season are >=5% below prior 5-year average in FAO/USDA data; NO otherwise.
resolution_rule_fixed: YES if Southern African maize yields for 2026/27 season are >=5% below prior 5-year average in FAO/USDA data; NO otherwise.
notes: Could in second sentence ignored; Medium–High on outlook→0.70 for yield stress.

claim_verbatim: In response to the 2026 reagent and climate shocks, the deployment of capital-intensive agricultural technologies is likely to accelerate rapidly.
source: Essay: War, El Niño, Pestilence, and Famine
resolution_criterion: YES if global precision-ag / AgTech capex or adoption metrics show clear acceleration in 2026–27 vs 2023–25 trend; NO if flat/down.
resolution_rule_fixed: YES if global precision-ag / AgTech capex or adoption metrics show clear acceleration in 2026–27 vs 2023–25 trend; NO if flat/down.

claim_verbatim: Copper is likely going past $15,000, but if you are an acid-dependent producer, your market cap might go down.
context: Price level in his own voice. The market-cap clause is a might and is not scored.
source: Essay: Why Sulphuric Acid Commands the Upstream Chokepoint of Civilisation
resolution_criterion: YES if LME copper cash or 3-month prints at or above USD 15,000/t (official settlement or a documented intraday high) on any day from 2026-04-22 through 2027-04-21 inclusive; NO otherwise. Prints on or before 2026-04-21 do not count.
resolution_rule_fixed: YES if LME copper cash or 3-month prints at or above USD 15,000/t (official settlement or a documented intraday high) on any day from 2026-04-22 through 2027-04-21 inclusive; NO otherwise. Prints on or before 2026-04-21 do not count.
resolution_source_planned: LME official copper prices, cash or 3-month
mechanism: Upstream sulphuric-acid dependency in SX-EW copper and HPAL nickel. Acid scarcity is the industrial constraint he ties to the copper price.
notes: Additional pass, not in batch 1. No date in the sentence; window fixed at 12 months, the same undated price-call window as batch 1. LME cash on 21 Apr 2026 was about USD 13,200.5/t (Westmetall daily table). Intraday 3-month high about USD 14,875/t on 10 Sep 2026 (ING Think) and about USD 14,617.5/t on 8 Oct 2026 (Bloomberg via Moneyweb). Still under 15,000, so open. No dated consensus probability at or before 21 Apr 2026 was found. The 'might go down' market-cap clause is not scored.
